title: Rectangular observations for finite matrix gradients: critical budgets and the weak endpoint
abstract: For a finite periodic lattice and arbitrary finite symmetric matrices acting on its actual forward gradient stack, we construct a coefficient-only partition into integer rectangles whose normalized component means restore coercivity with output dimension O_D(h(1+F_c(A))). The finite quadratic penalty may depend on the entire coefficient profile, including its negative spectral depth. Positive spectral replacement, a complete scalar balanced-ring BV and weighted-gap construction, and singleton refinement at affected starts and forward endpoints derive the result. A positive diagonal family shows worst-case product order hF_c(A) is necessary for common partitions retaining every component mean on the all-field domain. At the scalar inverse-D/2 weak endpoint, finite layer cake gives a logarithmic upper bound, and explicit actual flat coexact fields force matching worst-case logarithmic dimension for centered differentiable observations with locally quadratic upper penalties. All proofs are included. The mechanisms are classical; historical priority and exact non-equivalence to classical approximation theory remain unestablished. No interacting/covariant producer, variable-weight curl identity, continuum theorem or physical mass gap follows.
